newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr may need consolidation before new run.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr may need consolidation before new run.

text.p: The U.S. dollar may need to consolidate at current levels before launching a new attack on loftier heights, analysts said on Frisday.
Late Friday, the dollar was quoted at 116.41/46 yen versus 115.68/78 late Thursday in New York, at 1.5670/80 marks vs 1.5437/47, and at 1.3588/98 Swiss francs vs 1.3475/85.

After substantial gains, the dollar is now eyeing tough resistance at 1.5735 marks, 117.75 yen and 1.3700 Swiss francs -- levels that call for solid consolidation before fresh momentum is gathered for a new daunting bull run, analysts stressed.
Beside the need for consolidation, analysts also cited uncertainty about the resumption of trading on Monday in Tokyo where markets were closed for a full week for the New Year holiday.

"We will see what happens on Monday," said Kevin Harris, senior currency analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch. "Japanese do not like to buy at the high. They are patient and will wait until the dollar dips near the lows of the day before they come in."
A temporary dollar pullback, however, is expected to leave key support levels well protected at 1.5595 marks, 115.80 yen and 1.3520 Swiss francs.
Harris also noted another factor adding to anxiety.
"A lot of these guys are going to come in at levels they have never seen in their trading lives," Harris said, in reference to the fresh 45-month high dollar/yen is quoted at.
"Dollar/mark will turn sour, though not for very long," added Harris who pointed out the nearly 2-1/2-pfennig gain on Friday was the biggest one-day rise on that exchange rate since August of 1995.
Harris also stressed the dollar's near-term fate is tied to the performance of U.S. financial assets which may suffer from a negative psychology if Japan's Nikkei index falters.
Failure to break through 1.5735 marks may result in range trading for a while with 1.5595 providing a floor.
But this may, in turn, prop up mark/yen back above 75.35 resistance and create the conditions for renewed dollar/yen strength above 117.75 -- paving the way for a run at 118.50.
Yen weakness could also allow cable -- which protected support at $1.6835 well -- to renew an attack on $1.7010.
